The Characters Are Expendable Assets. The trickster needs dangerous tasks accomplished and is unwilling to send their more experienced agents out of concern those agents might not return. The characters’ deaths won’t inconvenience the trickster.

Trickster Patrons

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.UmzBAV49oQEDc4ou classes="float-right overlay-caption size-two" cite=false]

The following characters from the D&D multiverse, all briefly described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide, could serve as trickster patrons:

Queen of Air and Darkness. The Queen of Air and Darkness is a foreboding and mysterious archfey who rules the Gloaming Court, a Domain of Delight in the Feywild. She favors followers who are willful and follow their instincts, obeying no laws. She’s likely to give the characters total freedom to choose how to accomplish their missions.

Summer Queen. Titania, the Summer Queen, is a benevolent figure, but she nonetheless displays all the whimsical arbitrariness of other archfey. The Summer Court is infamous for its elaborate rules of behavior; characters working for Titania inevitably break unstated rules, prompting Titania to assign them punishments that lead to further adventures.

Tasha. Tasha, the adopted daughter of Baba Yaga, is a mighty spellcaster who authored the Demonomicon and invented several famous spells. Tasha has a unique relationship with fate, having been a tyrant known as Iggwilv, the Witch Queen of Perrenland; a planes-walking archmage; and Zybilna, archfey of the domain of Prismeer. You can learn more about Tasha in The Wild Beyond the Witchlight. Her mysterious goals could lead the characters anywhere in the multiverse.

Creating Your Own Trickster

Instead of using one of the tricksters described above, you can create a trickster to serve as a group patron for your characters.

A trickster group patron is whimsical, entertaining, and funny. However, a little whimsy goes a long way. Your trickster should focus their practical jokes and pranks on rivals and enemies, not the characters, or the party will soon find the trickster tiresome rather than amusing. Ensure that the trickster (mostly) tells the truth to the characters while maintaining a sense of humor and indulging the characters’ pranks and jests.

When you create a trickster for your campaign, you can roll on or choose from the Trickster Type table to determine their nature.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunTricksterTyY2 rollable resultLabel="Patron Type" captionPosition=top]{Trickster Type}

Trickster Patron Perks

Characters in a party whose patron is a trickster gain the following perks.

Compensation. A trickster group patron pays you as a way of binding you to them and ensuring your continued loyalty. On average, the trickster pays each member of your group 4 GP per day (enough to sustain a Wealthy lifestyle). They might bestow additional gifts such as gemstones, art objects, or Common or Uncommon magic items on you on completion of a successful mission. However, the trickster might withhold this money and reclaim gifts if you displease them or refuse an onerous mission.

Fickle Friends. The trickster has formed many surprising relationships in their travels across the multiverse, and they can call upon unexpected allies to aid your missions. These allies are often otherworldly—including devils, demons, fey, and stranger creatures—but they are always Friendly while aiding you (though not necessarily afterward). The trickster can call on these friends to secure transportation for you by a means of your choosing (via coach, ship, or teleportation) at half the usual cost. When you take a Bastion turn, if you are level 9+, you can (as a group) issue the Recruit order to the trickster as if they were a Teleportation Circle facility in your Bastion.

Resources. The trickster has a vast collection of dangerous relics, magic items, spellbooks, and other resources collected over a long lifetime. You can call in a favor to gain access to these resources. Additionally, you can consult with the trickster or their more powerful associates, if you’re willing to risk their attention.

Strange Gifts. The trickster grants your group a small measure of esoteric power. At level 5, and again at level 13, you each gain one supernatural gift as described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. The DM determines which supernatural gifts are available.

Trickster Contacts

Deception is key to the trickster group patron, and a trickster is likely to meet with the characters personally while concealing their identity. But not all tricksters can disguise themselves, and the disguise falls away once the trickster finds the joke has worn stale. Tricksters instead might communicate with the characters through various other means, including agents, spells, or magic items.

If the trickster uses an agent, roll on or choose from the Trickster Contact table to determine who manages the relationship between the characters and the trickster.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunTricksterCoKz rollable resultLabel="Contact Type" captionPosition=top]{Trickster Contact}

A Trickster Campaign

A campaign driven by a trickster patron might unfold according to this outline:

Levels 1–4. The trickster recruits the characters while concealing their own identity and tests the characters by pitting them against lesser Fey such as bullywugs, goblins, and worgs in service to a coven of @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGreenHag000000]{Green Hags}.

Levels 5–10. The characters have earned the grudging respect of the trickster, who sends them into the Feywild on missions that emphasize exploration and interaction. The party is tasked with stealing a bauble the trickster favors or persuading two of the trickster’s enemies to fight each other.

Levels 11–16. The trickster’s enemies catch up with them, and the characters must protect their patron from demons, adult dragons, and mortal archmages, all of whom have longstanding grudges against the trickster.

Levels 17–20. The characters discover the enemies fighting the trickster are being subtly manipulated by a villainous Arch-hag that seeks to supplant the trickster and seize their role. To end the threat, the characters must corner the hag in its lair.

Wizards’ Circle.name: Wizards’ Circle
Wizards’ Circle.text:
Powerful spellcasters occasionally form an alliance known as a wizards’ circle to pursue goals beyond the reach of any individual. Wizards’ circles are often temporary, formed to resolve a specific problem that threatens the world or the multiverse. But even archmages need friends or allies, and the members of a wizards’ circle might make their alliance permanent.

In many ways, a wizards’ circle is like an archmage group patron, with the added complication that the circle consists of several strong-willed individuals who don’t necessarily like each other. The characters get caught in the middle of long debates and old rivalries between members of the circle, and it can be hard to satisfy one member of the circle without alienating another.

Wizards’ Circle Motivations

A wizards’ circle might patronize a group for the following reasons:

The Characters Balance Each Other. Each member of the wizards’ circle has their own preferences when selecting agents and operatives. The party represents a collection of these preferences, with each member of the circle backing one member of the party. Although each character is backed by a single member, the circle as a whole serves as a group patron for the characters.

The Characters Have Special Skills. A wizards’ circle lacks expertise in fields outside members’ specialties, including types of magic outside their bailiwick, martial prowess, or exploration skills. The characters provide useful abilities that the circle members lack.

Pawns on the Chessboard. The wizards’ circle supports the group because the characters feature in the circle’s long-term plans. The circle members might know one of the characters is unknowingly a noble and thus a potential candidate for the throne, or they might have identified one of the characters as the only person who can safely wield a dangerous Artifact. These facts might not be known to the characters.

Wizards’ Circle Patrons

The following organizations could serve as wizards’ circle group patrons:

Circle of Eight. The Circle of Eight is an alliance of powerful spellcasters that includes the gnome Bigby; the humans Jallarzi Sallavarian, Mordenkainen, and Otiluke; and the dwarf Otto, all briefly described in the Dungeon Master’s Guide. The Circle is based in the world of Greyhawk and concerns itself with maintaining the power balance between Oerth’s realms and factions. The Circle of Eight favors neutral-aligned agents and avoids attention, preferring to work behind the scenes.

Order of the Many-Starred Cloak. The Order of the Many-Starred Cloak is dedicated to defending and supporting Neverwinter, a city in the Forgotten Realms. In the past, the order has protected the city from rival mages in nearby Luskan, among other threats. Members include powerful mages such as the human Gallio Elibro, who’s known for his planar research. The order might hire characters to investigate threats against the city, such as monsters amassed near Neverwinter or cults ensconced in the city.

Wizards Three. The wizard Alustriel Silverhand called on her friends Tasha and Mordenkainen to thwart one of Vecna’s plots. This alliance is known as the Wizards Three, and it is detailed in Vecna: Eve of Ruin. In that adventure, one of the Wizards Three isn’t who they appear to be; you might continue this deception or decide the three wizards continue their alliance once Vecna is defeated.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.Z0Zuu5gyi7i6mBeU classes=overlay-caption cite=false]

Creating Your Own Wizards’ Circle

Instead of using one of the wizards’ circles described above, you can create a wizards’ circle to serve as a group patron for your characters. You can use several of the archmage stat blocks in chapter 6, each of which specializes in one school of magic. If your world has a mages’ guild, discussed earlier in this chapter, that guild might make an excellent wizards’ circle group patron.

To make your own wizards’ circle, start by creating one circle member for each of the player characters; this member acts as a personal patron to that character, while the circle as a whole supports the party’s activities. For example, if one of your players has created a Sorcerer with the Draconic Sorcery subclass, the circle might include a dragon who has chosen the sorcerer as their personal agent. Other circle members, however, support different characters, and these members are the dragon’s rivals.

When you create a wizards’ circle for your campaign, you can roll on or choose from the Wizards’ Circle Type table.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunWizardsCircHn rollable resultLabel="Patron Type" captionPosition=top]{Wizards' Circle Type}

Wizards’ Circle Patron Perks

Characters in a party whose patron is a wizards’ circle gain the following perks.

Assisting Apprentices. The wizards in the circle have trained numerous apprentices, many of whom are loyal to their mentor. Whenever you’re in a city, a former apprentice of a circle member can cast any level 1 or lower spell at no cost, as long as you identify yourself as an agent of that circle member. A former apprentice can cast any level 2–8 spell for you at half the usual cost, as long as you’re in a city and similarly identify yourself.

Compensation. The wizards’ circle pays you to complete tasks on the circle’s behalf. On average, the wizards’ circle pays each member of your group 2 GP per day (enough to sustain a Comfortable lifestyle). Or you might be paid (at least 300 GP) after completing each task the wizards’ circle assigns.

Magical Resources. The wizards’ circle has collected untold magic items and magical curiosities. This collection is scattered among the sanctums of the circle members. A wizards’ circle can give members of the group any Common or Uncommon magic item in the Dungeon Master’s Guide, as long as possession of the item would help the group’s tasks. When the characters reach level 11, the wizards’ circle can retrieve one Rare and one Very Rare magic item in between the group’s tasks and award it to them as additional compensation. When the characters reach level 17, the wizards’ circle can retrieve one Rare, Very Rare, or Legendary magic item in between tasks and award it to the group as additional compensation.

Safe Houses. The wizards’ circle maintains magically warded safe houses and hiding spots throughout the world or across multiple worlds. Your group knows how to locate these hidden redoubts and can sustain a Modest lifestyle in one for no cost. Revealing the location of one of these safe houses, whether purposefully or by accident, causes you to lose favor with the wizards’ circle, and you might be banned from using them.

Wizards’ Circle Contacts

The members of a wizards’ circle don’t always agree, and they keep secrets from each other. An individual in the circle might meet with only one or two characters at a time, in secret. In addition, the circle as a whole has an official spokesperson who communicates with the characters and gives them tasks.

Roll on or choose from the Wizards’ Circle Contact table to determine who manages the relationship between the characters and the wizards’ circle.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunWizardsCirccM rollable resultLabel="Contact Type" captionPosition=top]{Wizards' Circle Contact}

A Wizards’ Circle Campaign

A campaign driven by a wizards’ circle patron might unfold according to this outline:

Levels 1–4. Each character in the group is selected by a single member of the wizards’ circle and brought together to serve the circle. Early missions pit the group against opposing @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMageApprentice]{Mage Apprentices}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmNothic00000000]{Nothics}, and other magical threats.

Levels 5–10. When the characters seek to recover magical lore, obtain dangerous Artifacts, or slay magical foes, sometimes the object of their quest is missing or has already fled. It slowly becomes clear that someone inside the circle is feeding information to the circle’s enemies.

Levels 11–16. The traitorous member of the circle reveals themself and seizes control of the circle and its resources. Other members of the circle are imprisoned, slain, bought off, or cowed into working with the traitor. The characters might play along for a while or go on the run, but eventually they must confront the traitor and their allies.

Levels 17–20. Now that the traitorous member of the circle is dealt with, the circle has openings for new members. The characters join the circle, recruiting new agents and rounding up the traitor’s remaining followers.

Magical Group Patrons.name: Magical Group Patrons
Magical Group Patrons.text:
Whether your heroes wish to advance the agenda of a famous mage or seek access to a magical academy’s ample resources, a group patron with significant magical prowess can create the cohesion that holds a campaign together and help your game feel infused with magic.

This section presents six types of magical group patrons around which you can create campaigns, as summarized on the Magical Patron Options table.

Each sample patron includes examples from the D&D multiverse and outlines for patronage campaigns. You can incorporate these into your game or use them as inspiration for your own magical group patron.

This section also explores the option of your group’s patron hiding their identity for reasons benevolent or malign, which can be used with any of the group patrons that follow.

Magical Patron Options

Category

Description

Archmage

A powerful, often famous mage with clear goals that span the multiverse

Esoteric institution

An organization dedicated to education, research, or containing dangerous magic

Magical entity

A non-Humanoid mage or magical creature with a mysterious, timeless outlook

Political faction

A group of powerful, like-minded mages deeply invested in political goals

Trickster

A capricious individual with inscrutable motives and a malevolent or whimsical nature

Wizards’ circle

An alliance of mages focused on pursuing a difficult goal or resolving a problem or threat

Magical Creatures.name: Magical Creatures
Magical Creatures.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.20VPAgjDMrXxLyzt classes=overlay-caption cite=false]

Use the following creatures to populate your magic-themed campaigns. Consult the Monster Manual for additional details on monsters. Creatures are presented here in alphabetical order.

Ninth Quill.name: Ninth Quill
Ninth Quill.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.eQM496Ux0ZS1dmS1 classes=overlay-caption cite=false]

The Ninth Quill is a faction of thieves, saboteurs, and spies who use magic to obtain and sequester powerful artifacts and knowledge by any means necessary—including robbing and sabotaging other factions. The faction’s leaders consider their organization to be superior to factions focused on a specific school of magic and the safest custodian of dangerous lore and relics, but some members also steal valuables and undermine other organizations for personal gain.

Goals and Activities.name: Goals and Activities
Goals and Activities.text:
Ninth Quill members’ adaptability and diverse areas of expertise help them infiltrate other groups, often posing as new recruits or long-absent members from other lands.

The Ninth Quill has a few popular catchphrases that members use as meaningful mantras—or excuses for criminality. These phrases are described in the sections that follow.

Our Hands Are Safest

Ninth Quill members often steal magic items and research to keep them out of others’ hands. They receive extensive training in handling dangerous artifacts and resisting the influence of sentient objects. In principle, these items are sequestered in the Ninth Quill vaults (which members insist are more secure than any other faction’s), but less scrupulous members might keep certain items for their own use.

Others Learn So We Can Earn

When the Ninth Quill steals discoveries and relics that aren’t particularly harmful, it sells them to wealthy patrons to fund its operations. Desperate buyers rebuffed by other factions, such as a necromancer rejected by the Covenant of the Grave or a transmuter suspicious of the Bringers of Cosmic Dawn, might seek the services of the Ninth Quill to obtain such objects.

Discontent Is Our Best Defense

The Ninth Quill seeks to destabilize other factions that become too powerful. This often involves agents infiltrating a faction, then undertaking whisper campaigns, sabotaging experiments, and encouraging critical personnel to depart. The Ninth Quill agents quietly slip away once they have stoked sufficient inefficiency, paranoia, and infighting.

Leadership and Organization.name: Leadership and Organization
Leadership and Organization.text:
The Ninth Quill values intelligence, resourcefulness, and loyalty. A significant majority of Ninth Quill agents use spellcasting to enhance their spy craft.

A Careful Hierarchy

Although Ninth Quill leaders take pains to hide their identities, the faction operates under a strict hierarchal system. Agents are the lowest ranking, followed by Lieutenants, followed by Masters. Those in the highest echelon are Guild Masters.

Joining the Ninth Quill

The Ninth Quill operates in the shadows and therefore doesn’t entertain applicants. However, the Guild Masters keep an eye on talented thieves and other morally ambiguous individuals with magical skills. If the Guild Masters believe such an individual would be an asset to the Ninth Quill, they extend an invitation to visit Blackscript College—through an anonymous courier, of course.

Blackscript College

The hidden academy where the Ninth Quill trains its members is located in a crime-ridden neighborhood of a busy trade city. Dilapidated warehouses, all owned by the Ninth Quill, surround the college to ensure its privacy. There’s no readily apparent entrance; instead, it’s accessible only by unmarked doors in twisting alleys and hidden passages.

The centuries-old college was once a legitimate magical academy, but city records show that it closed decades ago due to administrative corruption. In truth, the college simply went underground to teach magical spy craft and thievery.

A former instructor at Blackscript College’s predecessor academy, the college’s dean is the elf Sirethe Slipshadow (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmSpyMaster00000]{Spy Master}). Slipshadow is infamous for her ability to impersonate others and uses these skills to observe students during their studies and on early missions.

The college’s library, called the Repository, holds an eclectic variety of stolen treasures. An adjacent chamber called the Ersatz Repository contains worktables where members make high-quality counterfeits of spellbooks, relics, and artifacts. Many cherished treasures held by other factions are actually Ninth Quill counterfeits.

Renown Rewards.name: Renown Rewards
Renown Rewards.text:
Characters gain renown with the Ninth Quill by completing Ninth Quill missions or by contributing stolen magical lore or magic items. As their Renown Scores increase, characters gain access to various perks, as shown on the Ninth Quill Renown table. If your campaign doesn’t use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

Ninth Quill Renown

Renown Score

Reward

3+

You and your companions receive free lodging at Ninth Quill safe houses, which are present in many cities.

5+

You can buy Common potions and Spell Scrolls from Ninth Quill members.

10+

If the authorities are searching for you, the Ninth Quill dispatches numerous faction members who are magically disguised to look like you. This might allow you to evade capture for days or months, at the DM’s discretion. Once you use this reward, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score increases.

15

The first time your Renown Score reaches 15, the Ninth Quill gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Repository.

20+

You receive a magical decoder that allows you to read written @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgeThievesCan]{Thieves’ Cant}. If your Renown Score drops below 20, this decoder is confiscated.

25+

The Ninth Quill can provide you with a believable but useless duplicate of a magic item you show them. Creating the duplicate takes [[/r1d4]] days of work. Once you use this reward, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score increases.

30

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, Ninth Quill faction members teach you how to magically shroud yourself. You always have the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplNondetecti]{Nondetection} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

40+

You can buy Uncommon and Rare potions and Spell Scrolls from Ninth Quill members.

50

The first time your Renown Score reaches 50, the Ninth Quill gives you a Very Rare magic item that another faction desperately wants to recover.

Ninth Quill Characters.name: Ninth Quill Characters
Ninth Quill Characters.text:
The Ninth Quill uses thieves and enforcers, but the group is no mere criminal guild; its leaders prefer recruits who have magical skill or knowledge.

The most welcome are @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrdBard000000]{Bards}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbftrFighter000]{Fighters} (especially those with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbftrEldritchKn]{Eldritch Knight} subclass), @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgeRogue00000]{Rogues} (especially those with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgeArcaneTric]{Arcane Trickster} subclass), @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwlkWarlock000]{Warlocks}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwzdWizard0000]{Wizards}. Characters with proficiency in Arcana or Deception; the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.backgrounds.Item.aunNinthQuillCpT]{Agent of the Ninth Quill} (see chapter 1), @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.origins.Item.phbbgCharlatan00]{Charlatan}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.origins.Item.phbbgCriminal000]{Criminal} background; or the Magic Initiate feat are also valued.

Member Benefits

If you’re a member of the Ninth Quill, you receive these benefits.

Modest Lifestyle. The Ninth Quill pays you a stipend to support your Modest lifestyle (1 GP per day).

Trinket. Roll on the Ninth Quill Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Ninth Quill.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunNinthQuillTrt rollable resultLabel="Trinket" captionPosition=top]{Ninth Quill Trinkets}

Using This Faction.name: Using This Faction
Using This Faction.text:
The Ninth Quill often opposes other magical factions. You might introduce Ninth Quill @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmBandit00000000]{Bandits} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmScout000000000]{Scouts} looking to steal the characters’ hard-won items or lore, or you could establish intrigue-laden plots about Ninth Quill @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmSpy00000000000]{Spies}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmSpyMaster00000]{Spy Masters}, or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmBanditDeceiver]{Bandit Deceivers} who stoke rivalries and paranoia within another faction.

Alternatively, the Ninth Quill could employ or aid the characters. The faction might recruit the characters to retrieve a valuable asset or assist them with recovering and disposing of a dangerous artifact. You could even build a campaign around efforts to steal relics from each of the other magical factions.

Good intentions are commonplace among members of the Ninth Quill, but never drop your guard around them.

Special Facility.name: Special Facility
Special Facility.text:
Members of the Ninth Quill can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.bastions.Item.aunHeistPlanning]{Heist Planning Chamber}

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.bastions.Item.aunHeistPlanning caption=false cite=false]

Phantasmic Circus.name: Phantasmic Circus
Phantasmic Circus.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.0pqEaR8sfss8bVx5 classes=overlay-caption cite=false]

Part entertainers’ alliance and part traveling carnival, the Phantasmic Circus is an organization of performers and illusionists who create grand spectacles and share magical techniques to delight, entertain, and misdirect.

Goals and Activities.name: Goals and Activities
Goals and Activities.text:
The Phantasmic Circus stages elaborate performances across the world, moving from city to city to bring delight and wonder. These performances are huge extravaganzas involving dozens of entertainers and drawing large audiences. The circus is renowned for illusions and pyrotechnics that reach hundreds of feet into the air.

These complex routines change with every show; Phantasmic Circus performers are always experimenting with new illusions, death-defying stunts, and musical accompaniment. Tickets and concessions are pricey, but audience members remember the faction’s thrilling spectacles for the rest of their lives.

The Phantasmic Circus’s performances use trained creatures for certain acts, but audience members would be shocked to realize how few genuine creatures are on display. Lifelike illusions of animals and monsters perform most stunts, while living animals are treated carefully and kept out of danger.

One Circus, Many Troupes

The Phantasmic Circus isn’t a single traveling troupe, but rather the collective name for several groups that operate independently, each under the guidance of a manager called a Wondermaker. Circus members might shift from group to group to hone their skills, so residents of a city might never realize that the “Phantasmic Circus” that visited twice the previous year was actually two different troupes.

Leadership and Organization.name: Leadership and Organization
Leadership and Organization.text:
The astounding and popular Phantasmic Circus of today had humble beginnings as a small traveling carnival called the Hayver and Hayver Circus. When the Hayvers’ youngest sibling, the human Della, returned to the family circus with training in Illusion magic and a gregarious gnome husband named Walnip Waddlebell, the circus started its meteoric rise.

Soon, Della and Walnip were running the circus as its ringmasters and self-appointed “First Maestros.” The couple also gave the increasingly illusion-focused show a flashier name. The other Hayvers have since passed away, but the aging First Maestros (both Small @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformerLegen]{Performer Legend}s), still plan spectacles, train new illusionists, and orchestrate the many troupes operating as the Phantasmic Circus.

Wondermakers

The First Maestros are now too old to tour, but they keep in touch with each troupe as its travels bring it back to the circus’s headquarters, the Mirage Lyceum. The First Maestros appoint a Wondermaker to guide each troupe. Most Wondermakers are flashy showoffs or grand illusionists who enjoy the spotlight as ringmasters or star performers. In other troupes, the Wondermaker works behind the scenes, guiding the performers and pushing their shows to new heights.

Each Wondermaker keeps their troupe’s books, protects its members, makes its travel plans, and coordinates with other Wondermakers to ensure they aren’t revisiting cities too soon. They also send performers from troupe to troupe to teach gifted members additional skills or to resolve personality clashes.

Roustabouts

Although acrobats, illusionists, animals, and entertainers are the stars of the Phantasmic Circus, a platoon of supporters keeps the troupe running. Collectively called roustabouts, these laborers and guides let the performers take the glory while collecting reasonable pay from the troupe’s Wondermaker. The visual artists who design the elaborate sets and costumes are also roustabouts; they mentor each other to hone their artistic skills.

Circus Acts

No two Phantasmic Circus performances are the same. Roll on the Phantasmic Circus Acts table to generate a sample act as a basis for other wondrous spectacles.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunPhantasmicCro rollable resultLabel="Circus Act" captionPosition=top]{Phantasmic Circus Acts}

Joining the Phantasmic Circus

Joining the Phantasmic Circus as a performer requires rigorous tryouts under the watchful eye of a troupe’s Wondermaker, who makes final decisions about applicants. Those who wish to join the circus as roustabouts, however, need only express interest and demonstrate a relevant skill to a Wondermaker, who is usually happy to accept the additional help.

Mirage Lyceum

The headquarters of the Phantasmic Circus, the Mirage Lyceum, was formerly the winter home of the Hayver and Hayver Circus. Once a sad collection of animal pens and bunk rooms, it is now a vibrant jumble of playhouses, amphitheaters, classrooms, and studios.

The Mirage Lyceum puts on informal performances year-round. Some performers simply want to show their skills to the First Maestros; others are junior members who aren’t yet ready to take to the road. This mingling of eager pupils and wise mentors makes the Mirage Lyceum an excellent place for any illusionist to learn.

Audiences come from miles around to view these informal performances, which are cheaper than the big-city spectacles. Some wonder-struck visitors stay for long periods, and a few become inspired to join the circus life.

Mystra smiles on those who pluck the Weave to provide entertainment to the public. So do I—as long as that entertainment cloaks no foul deeds.

Renown Rewards.name: Renown Rewards
Renown Rewards.text:
Characters gain renown with the Phantasmic Circus by contributing illusory spectacles or by completing missions for the circus. As their Renown Scores increase, they gain access to various perks, as shown on the Phantasmic Circus Renown table. If your campaign doesn’t use renown, the DM decides if and when characters earn these perks.

Phantasmic Circus Renown

Renown Score

Reward

3+

You can travel with the Phantasmic Circus, receiving food and cramped lodging (a Poor lifestyle) while you do. You can attend performances for free.

5+

After a performance, faction members freely share with you [[/r 1d6]] rumors heard from the audience members.

10

The first time your Renown Score reaches 10, the Phantasmic Circus gives you an Uncommon magic item from the Wand or Wondrous Item category.

15+

A troupe of [[/r 1d3 + 1]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformer00000]{Performers} become your loyal followers. The troupe performs simple tasks, such as restocking supplies or gathering information, but they won’t willingly put themselves in danger.

20+

You can buy Common and Uncommon Spell Scrolls that contain Illusion spells from faction members.

25+

Your troupe gains an additional [[/r 1d4]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformer00000]{Performers} . Additionally, you can ask your troupe to help you with one dangerous mission. Once you use this reward, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score increases.

30

The first time your Renown Score reaches 30, circus members share their illusory tricks with you. You always have the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMirrorImag]{Mirror Image} spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you gain this reward). You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

40+

You can arrange for a meeting with any of the faction’s Wondermakers or, when at the Mirage Lyceum, with the First Maestros. Once you use this reward, you can’t do so again until your Renown Score increases.

50+

[[/r 1d4]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformerMaest]{Performer Maestros} and an additional [[/r 1d6]] @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformer00000]{Performers} join your troupe.

Phantasmic Circus Characters.name: Phantasmic Circus Characters
Phantasmic Circus Characters.text:
The Phantasmic Circus welcomes artists, entertainers, and illusionists of all types as performers, provided they impress a Wondermaker. Roustabouts can be of any class or background.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbbrdBard000000]{Bards}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbrgeRogue00000]{Rogues}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwzdWizard0000]{Wizards} (especially those with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.classes.Item.phbwzdIllusionis]{Illusionist} subclass) are excellent fits, as are characters with proficiency in Performance or with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.origins.Item.phbbgCharlatan00]{Charlatan}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.origins.Item.phbbgEntertainer]{Entertainer}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.backgrounds.Item.aunPhantasmicCVc]{Phantasmic Circus Trouper }(see chapter 1), or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.origins.Item.phbbgWayfarer000]{Wayfarer} background.

Member Benefits

If you’re a member of the Phantasmic Circus, you receive these benefits.

Patron Connections. You can always find work as an entertainer while in a settlement.

Poor Lifestyle. The circus provides you with performance proceeds to support your Poor lifestyle (2 SP per day).

Trinket. Roll on the Phantasmic Circus Trinkets table to determine what trinket you have from your time with the Phantasmic Circus.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunPhantasmicCgu rollable resultLabel="Trinket" captionPosition=top]{Phantasmic Circus Trinkets}

Using This Faction.name: Using This Faction
Using This Faction.text:
You can use the Phantasmic Circus in your campaign to enliven an urban atmosphere. Since the Phantasmic Circus travels from city to city, the characters also might encounter the faction on the road.

The Phantasmic Circus cares more about presenting grand spectacles than following local laws. As such, the circus might create inadvertent fires or spark a panicked stampede that requires the characters’ intervention. Alternatively, the circus might agree to conceal fugitives who don’t seem harmful, possibly enabling the party to escape a settlement without alerting the authorities.

Special Facility.name: Special Facility
Special Facility.text:
Members of the Phantasmic Circus can add the following special facility to their Bastions.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.bastions.Item.aunCircusTent000]{Circus Tent}

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.bastions.Item.aunCircusTent000 caption=false cite=false]

Seers of Sea and Sky.name: Seers of Sea and Sky
Seers of Sea and Sky.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.1lWEiJ3xZzXCP8kZ classes=overlay-caption cite=false]

The Seers of Sea and Sky is a faction of oracles who make predictions about the future based on movements of the clouds and waves. Open to all methods of divination, the seers encourage communication with a wide array of aerial and undersea prophets and meticulously record their prognostications.

Goals and Activities.name: Goals and Activities
Goals and Activities.text:
The Seers of Sea and Sky maintains libraries and reading rooms in many large, coastal cities. Within these hubs, seers cast Divination spells for reasonable costs; train other members in divination techniques; and maintain contact with visionaries across, above, and below the seas. Although obtaining accurate information through divination is important to the faction, sharing knowledge and imparting guidance to those most in need of it is also a crucial part of the faction’s mission.

The seers primarily practice what they call hydromancy, or predictions based on watching the movement of water, and aeromancy, or predictions based on observing the weather. Members hone many subspecialties within these techniques. For example, some seers divine by scrutinizing driftwood delivered by ocean waves, while others base predictions on the movement of clouds.

Allies of Air and Water

Faction members live in diverse locales and include a wide array of folk. The faction’s membership includes aarakocra, giant eagles, and other flying creatures who can provide detailed data about the wind and cloud movement. Other seers live beneath the waves, including bronze dragons and merfolk. Members from both groups and land-bound seers often convene, keeping the faction cohesive.

Truth Twice

The seers maintain a philosophy they call “truth twice.” The faction doesn’t consider a prophecy or revelation to be reliable unless it’s been corroborated by another member—preferably one using a different Divination spell or method of divining. Checking and rechecking other members’ work is routine. As a result, the seers’ predictions have a reputation for reliability. The support members provide for each other contributes to the organization’s close-knit culture.

Leadership and Organization.name: Leadership and Organization
Leadership and Organization.text:
The oracles who founded the Seers of Sea and Sky were called the Scholars of Deep Truth. As the scholars’ fame spread and wealthy patrons sought their guidance, the scholars built an exclusive, opulent lighthouse to entertain petitioners. The scholars worked with undersea oracles to strengthen the accuracy of their own prophecies.

When several misleading prognostications left locals victims of suspicious seaside disasters, the scholars started questioning their sources. They soon discovered an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAboleth0000000]{Aboleth} named Naurishaul was manipulating them. Before the scholars could address this shocking news, a client exposed the scholars as minions of this malevolent undersea entity. While technically true, this announcement was misleading, as the scholars hadn’t realized their answers came from such a sinister source.

A New Beginning

The scandal could have driven the scholars into hiding or ruin, but the organization publicly acknowledged its unsavory association and resolved to do better. Members established a network of mutual education and support, teaching genuine divination methods and rigorously double-checking their revelations. They kept the remote lighthouse as the faction’s headquarters but established outposts to provide answers in seaside cities where petitioners of more limited means could seek guidance.

The efforts to rebuild the scholars’ reputation worked. Experts in hydromancy and aeromancy joined the faction, attracted by its openness and support. Many were diviners from far-flung places, including windswept peaks and undersea communities. To reflect the organization’s growing membership and shed its tainted legacy, the faction changed its name to the Seers of Sea and Sky.

Focused entirely on their divination mission, the seers eschew hierarchy. New members are expected to respect more senior members, but the faction in general has an egalitarian outlook. Beyond the Founders (see below), members consider titles and ranks unnecessary.

The Founders

The faction’s inner circle consists of the original Scholars of Deep Truth members, though they use that scandal-ridden name only as a cautionary tale. Other seers simply refer to them as the Founders. With a reputation for humility, insight, and rigor, the Founders are highly regarded throughout the faction.

The Founders consist of the human siblings Kessalee Cloudseeker and Narvok Cloudseeker (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMage0000000000]{Mages}), haughty elf Travieste Nilvinarian (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmNobleProdigy00]{Noble Prodigy}), and gregarious gnome Bulrug Seawhistle (Small @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformerMaest]{Performer Maestro}). The Founders frequently travel to consult with faction members scattered across land, sea, and air environments.

Wavewatchers

Some Seers of Sea and Sky have formed a coterie called the Wavewatchers. These members enjoy watching ocean waves crash against the shore, and they spend hours in contemplation, watching light play on the waves and listening to their soothing sounds. The Wavewatchers have created a meditation trend that attracts more faction members each week. A few of the newest faction members aren’t diviners at all—they’re mystics or monks who’ve joined to seek peace from the rolling waves.

However, some faction members have fallen behind in their work in favor of wave watching, and they’re producing unconfirmed divinations. This is unacceptable to the Founders, who are displeased with the Wavewatchers phenomenon. Kessalee worries that their old foe Naurishaul has infiltrated the faction once again by mesmerizing susceptible faction members.

Remarkable Members

Most members of the Seers of Sea and Sky are humanoids, but the Notable Seers table provides examples of unusual beings who have joined the faction.

Notable Seers

Name

Description

Gnarlbeak

Gnarlbeak, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGiantOwl000000]{Giant Owl} , survived a demon attack in her youth and has become an expert on predicting fiendish incursions by studying lightning storms.

Kaekylin

The sardonic, blue-feathered @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAarakocraAerom]{Aarakocra Aeromancer} Kaekylin is eager to discuss cloud formations.

Quellishar

An @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAdultBronzeDra]{Adult Bronze Dragon} , Quellishar can’t speak and uses graceful dances to communicate truths he sees in the movements of the tides.

Tuppet Seaclaw

Tuppet, a pensive @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmSeaHag00000000]{Sea Hag} , shares insights gained by watching schools of fish migrate; she’s understanding if clients are cautious about interacting with a hag.

Vort

The @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmWaterWeird0000]{Water Weird} Vort uses tide pools to perform scrying rituals.

Joining the Seers of Sea and Sky

Anyone with an interest in studying the sea or sky to gain insights can join the faction as a scribe or assistant for the diviners who perform the bulk of the faction’s work. Joining as a diviner is more difficult. Applicants must travel to the faction’s lighthouse and request membership from any senior member, who makes the final admission decision. Those who don’t qualify for membership are usually still welcome to stay at the lighthouse as guests.

Lighthouse Academy

The prior incarnation of the Seers of Sea and Sky, the Scholars of Deep Truth, renovated a sprawling lighthouse as an upscale retreat for wealthy petitioners. The lighthouse remains the seers’ headquarters and the Founders’ home, but it has been renovated to align to the seers’ new mission.

The Lighthouse Academy, as it’s now known, houses dozens. New members have built outbuildings around the lighthouse and equipped them with bunk rooms, scrying chambers, and libraries.

Few residents of the Lighthouse Academy work alone; daily mentoring and mutual confirmation of predictions keep the seers in close contact with each other. Shared living spaces here outnumber individual residences.

The seers employ lighthouse keepers who know little about divination but are experts in cleaning and operating the facility. To further repair their reputation, the Founders recently had these operators construct two smaller lighthouses on nearby promontories. The new lighthouses provide additional navigational guidance to sea travelers. Many captains in turn give seers free passage, citing the value of the lighthouses while secretly believing that no seer would seek passage on a ship that wasn’t destined to reach its destination safely.

Using This Faction.name: Using This Faction
Using This Faction.text:
The Seers of Sea and Sky are an excellent source of prophecies to steer a campaign. Faction members receive guidance from the natural world and freely share their divinations rather than hoard them. If the natural world is somehow at risk—for example, threatened by aberrations or fiends—the seers might be the first to know.

The faction can also answer specific questions the characters might have, like where to find a necessary item. The seers are precise and careful with their divinations and therefore trustworthy—but deciphering their enigmatic guidance might lead the characters on new adventures.

All of fate is written in the Weave, and few places on the Material Plane are closer to raw magic than the sea and sky. There is wisdom is seeking truths from these places.

Sheltering Hands.name: Sheltering Hands
Sheltering Hands.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.hMMdUYA64dM0zqUI classes=overlay-caption cite=false]

The Sheltering Hands is a benevolent organization of abjurers and advocates who operate emergency shelters and soup kitchens in far-flung settlements. This well-respected faction uses Abjuration magic to protect the vulnerable and remove afflictions.

Goals and Activities.name: Goals and Activities
Goals and Activities.text:
Sheltering Hands members are skilled abjurers who focus on providing services to the needy. Faction members solicit donations of food, money, or land, then share them in directed ways to reduce as much suffering as possible. They operate shelters, aid disease-stricken regions, and work to lift curses.

Beyond fulfilling immediate needs, members of the Sheltering Hands help individuals rebuild their dignity, security, and self-determination. Its members happily share bread with the hungry, but they also delight in helping the hungry set up communal farms and other enterprises so they can feed themselves. Members also work against despots to build community solidarity and create support programs that help marginalized populations voice their needs.

Abjurers of the Sheltering Hands also teach the rudiments of defensive magic to those who show interest and aptitude. Faction members who are mages lift curses and remove debilitating conditions; even members who can’t cast the appropriate spells usually know enough to recognize what spells are needed.

Many of those the faction helps become members themselves, seeking to pay forward the support they’ve received and prevent others from suffering as they did.

Balance of Faith

The Sheltering Hands isn’t a religious organization, though some of its members are priests and many venerate deities of mercy, charity, and self-sacrifice. The faction doesn’t favor any particular religion and welcomes good-hearted members of all sorts, including former followers of evil faiths who have renounced their earlier affiliations. This nonsectarian policy allows the Sheltering Hands to coordinate relief or rescue efforts across organizations.

Fieldwork

Instead of expecting those in need to journey to them, small teams of Sheltering Hands members travel to deliver food, refresh supplies, and cast Abjuration spells. Spells from other schools of magic are often useful to repair structures, produce a bounty from sickly crops, or chase away opportunistic predators, so teams often include spellcasters with specialties other than Abjuration.

Leadership and Organization.name: Leadership and Organization
Leadership and Organization.text:
The faction’s leadership council consists of five members. The council members make the hard decisions of allocating limited resources to do the most good.

The Leadership Council table presents the members of the faction’s leadership council. All are Lawful Good.

Leadership Council

Name

Council Member

Elbeezar Ghont

Elbeezar (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMage0000000000]{Mage} ), a human, comes from a farming village that supplies the faction’s soup kitchens.

Nylusk the Golden

Nylusk (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMage0000000000]{Mage} ), an orc, proudly walks with a limp earned while breaking up a riot.

Opener-of-Thought

Opener-of-Thought is a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmDeva0000000000]{Deva} who prefers the form of a placid orangutan.

Slade Margid

Slade (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmArchpriest0000]{Archpriest} ), who is a human, believes the organization should put more resources into helping communities form long-term solutions.

Zosh Curvin

Zosh (Small @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMage0000000000]{Mage} ), a halfling, believes the organization should focus on providing emergency aid rather than pursuing long-term solutions.

Dueling Priorities

Friction within the Sheltering Hands comes from disagreements about how the organization might best help those in need. Some members believe the Sheltering Hands should focus on providing emergency aid to those experiencing hardship. Others believe that while providing aid is important, the organization should focus more on providing resources to communities to address societal struggles that cause long-term suffering. Some tension exists between these two groups, each of whose members believe their priority is superior. This dispute was minor at first, but some Sheltering Hands members have started refusing to serve alongside those of the opposite group, throwing off the faction’s carefully planned administration.

Joining the Sheltering Hands

The Sheltering Hands welcomes all recruits interested in aiding the faction’s mission, whether by offering protection during a faction outing or providing spellcasting services.

Andarin’s Aegis

Andarin’s Aegis is a large academy located in the temple district of a bustling metropolis. The Sheltering Hands established the academy as a school where its members can learn more about Abjuration magic, but, consistent with Sheltering Hands impulses, it has been used when needed as a soup kitchen, an impromptu medical center, a veteran’s service center, and a shelter for children without homes. Its students are eager to learn from those who use Abjuration magic to aid others.

Andarin was one of the faction’s earliest council members. Centuries after his death, many members still cite his dedication to helping the unhoused, but fewer remember his innovative contributions to the corpus of Abjuration spells.

The academy’s dean is Malvanar Lumblin (Medium, Neutral Good @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAberrantCultis]{Aberrant Cultist}), a garrulous human who has reformed his wicked ways. Students hang on his words when he talks about the beholder cult he once served. Malvaner’s expertise about the antimagic nature of beholder eyes has proven revolutionary to abjurative studies.

You can involve the characters in faction rivalries between those who disagree about organizational priorities. Such conflicts can be compelling because both sides have good intentions and neither is a clear villain.

Arcana Domain (Cleric).name: Arcana Domain (Cleric)
Arcana Domain (Cleric).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.CuidH7gEuXldusCy classes="overlay-caption float-left size-three" cite=false]

Amplify Your Magical Power

Magic suffuses the multiverse and fuels both destruction and creation. Clerics with the Arcana Domain view magical knowledge not as power to be used in pursuit of personal ends, but as a gift they have the responsibility to share.

Gods associated with the Arcana Domain know the secrets and potential of magic intimately. These gods are often connected to knowledge, secrecy, or power.

Magic and the divine are naturally in harmony, like colors in a beautiful cosmic painting.

Arcane Archer (Fighter).name: Arcane Archer (Fighter)
Arcane Archer (Fighter).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.H9RTYR1M2bpknxjr classes="overlay-caption float-left size-four" cite=false]

Deploy Magical Effects Through Enchanted Ammunition

An Arcane Archer studies a unique elven method of archery that weaves magic into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Over the centuries, other folk have learned this technique and broadened it so it applies to ranged weapons of many kinds and to aspects of adventuring life outside of combat.

When Mystra guides your arrows, they seldom miss.

Warrior of the Mystic Arts (Monk).name: Warrior of the Mystic Arts (Monk)
Warrior of the Mystic Arts (Monk).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.Tb1OC4FTEDXbOE7V classes="overlay-caption float-left size-three" cite=false]

Weave Martial and Mystic Arts

Warriors of the Mystic Arts wield magic to supplement their martial skill. They harness mystical focus to enhance their magical and physical abilities.

Fists can be powerful. Magic makes them more so.

Vestige Patron (Warlock).name: Vestige Patron (Warlock)
Vestige Patron (Warlock).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.YCLKe0Lv63TTLmM3 classes="overlay-caption float-left size-three" cite=false]

Wield the Remnants of a Dying God’s Power

Your pact draws on the power of a dying god, a being once worshipped by countless followers but now abandoned and forgotten. This dying god, known as a vestige, might have been benevolent, evil, or strange and unknowable, but now it is driven to regain its former power. The vestige needs your help, and it is willing to share its remaining strength with you.

The multiverse is full of gods, though not all their names grace the halls of temples. Communing with a forgotten god’s benevolence is a noble pursuit.

Conjurer (Wizard).name: Conjurer (Wizard)
Conjurer (Wizard).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.2D5SFxo6DgbRbNJH classes="overlay-caption float-left size-three" cite=false]

Step Across Space and Call Creatures from Thin Air

A Conjurer considers distance and matter to be flexible guidelines rather than physical laws. Conjurers master magic that moves creatures instantly through space and summons creatures to fight on their behalf.

There is no concept of physical distance in the Weave. With enough magical power, you can travel anywhere in existence with merely a thought.

Enchanter (Wizard).name: Enchanter (Wizard)
Enchanter (Wizard).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.Sk74AdwKmYXOyAn4 classes="overlay-caption float-left size-three" cite=false]

Entrance and Beguile Others

An Enchanter’s magic clouds or captivates minds. Some Enchanters use their abilities to encourage peace and soften cruelty, while others use their mind-altering magic for selfish ends.

Minds can be molded like clay when magic is involved. Take care you don’t abuse this power.

Necromancer (Wizard).name: Necromancer (Wizard)
Necromancer (Wizard).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.8BIKoD4qDyVlBP4H classes="overlay-caption float-left size-three" cite=false]

Command the Powers of Death and Undeath

You explore the forces of life, death, and undeath. As a necromancer, you learn to manipulate the energy that animates all creatures, and you draw increasing power from the forbidden secrets in your spellbook. Though many see Necromancers as menacing or villainous, not all Necromancers are evil.

Minds can be molded like clay when magic is involved. Take you don't abuse this power.

Transmuter (Wizard).name: Transmuter (Wizard)
Transmuter (Wizard).description:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.QH36TqCLjz4xf1kl classes="overlay-caption float-left size-three" cite=false]

Transform Energy and Matter

You study spells that modify energy and matter—to you, the world is eminently mutable. Using your magic, you become a smith at reality’s forge.

Some Transmuters are tinkerers and pranksters. Others seek the power to make and destroy worlds.

Commune with the Weave, and the limitations of your corporeal form will begin to fall away.

Subclasses.name: Subclasses
Subclasses.text:
This chapter presents eight new subclasses that are particularly appropriate for characters in settings that emphasize magic:

Arcana Domain: A Cleric of a divine force who understands the secrets and potential of magic intimately

Arcane Archer: A Fighter who draws on a unique tradition of elven archery to weave magic into their attacks

Warrior of the Mystic Arts: A Monk who wields magic to supplement their martial skill

Vestige Patron: A Warlock who draws on the power of a dying god

Conjurer: A Wizard who has mastered the arts of teleportation and summoning spirit allies

Enchanter: A Wizard who has become an expert in clouding and captivating minds

Necromancer: A Wizard who can manipulate and draw magic from life, death, and undeath

Transmuter: A Wizard who has mastered modifying energy and matter

Mystra’s gifts range from subtle to earthshakingly powerful. Infuse your day with a little magic or stop a mighty villain from causing suffering—or both. When you study magic, your options are unlimited.

Taisus.name: Taisus
Taisus.text:
Magically Ascended Mage

Habitat: Any; Treasure: Arcana

The most gifted mortal mages can sometimes peer beyond reality to glimpse pure, untrammeled magic. Directly accessing this energy requires years of careful study and dangerous rituals. Any mage who succeeds taps into esoteric powers that strip away the mage’s physical body, blending their mortal mind with raw magic to form a quasi-corporeal entity called a taisus, or an ascended mage.

A taisus initially retains the personality and values of the mortal mage it was before, but its mindset eventually becomes alien, taking on a long-term outlook that seems callous to mortals. Most taisuses seek to draw energies from places of significant magical power, such as planar portals or quintessence pools, in order to create bizarre magic items, reshape the nature of magic, or lead others to duplicate their eldritch ascension. A taisus’s end goal is unfathomable to mortal minds.

Tomb of the Shadow Serpents.name: Tomb of the Shadow Serpents
Tomb of the Shadow Serpents.text:
@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.mYIKYMsEfRyidW1Z cite=false classes="adventure-cover"]

This adventure is designed to fill one or two sessions of play. It can take place in any region where there are forests and caves.

Import this Adventure: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.adventures.Adventure.lmF97bDlI9Bu554e]{Tomb of the Shadow Serpents}

Important Note: Links throughout this journal will appear broken unless it is imported.

Key Plot Points.name: Key Plot Points
Key Plot Points.text:
The following information is key to this adventure’s story:

Venger’s Schemes. The characters receive a mysterious missive from @UUID[Actor.aunVenger0000000]{Venger} (see @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunVenger6HdQcEk.JournalEntryPage.Vengerd0LNH2M8UT]{chapter 6}), a fiendish mage who invites them to plumb the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents in search of treasure. In reality, Venger wishes to test whether the characters would be useful tools for his schemes.

Escape the Tomb. The characters venture into the tomb and discover many fallen heroes who previously tried to claim Venger’s treasure. If the characters survive, they can keep the magic items they find, and they pique Venger’s interest. If they die, their bones will lie in the tomb forever.

Preparation.name: Preparation
Preparation.text:
Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:

Step 1. Read the “Adventure Background” section. Optionally, read the description of the Shadowfell in the Dungeon Master’s Guide or on D&D Beyond.

Step 2. Review area T12 and familiarize yourself with the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgShadowfellDes]{Shadowfell Despair} table in the Dungeon Master’s Guide’s description of the Shadowfell. If you find it too complicated to use the table’s effects in @UUID[.T12TheShadowySeM]{area T12}, feel free to skip them.

Step 3. Make a copy of the Serpent Puzzle Piece handouts. (You will share these with the other players at certain points during the adventure.)

Foundry Note

The Serpent Puzzle Pieces are included as items: @UUID[Item.aun1SerpentPuzzl]{Serpent Puzzle Piece 1}, @UUID[Item.aun2SerpentPuzzl]{Serpent Puzzle Piece 2}, @UUID[Item.aun3SerpentPuzzl]{Serpent Puzzle Piece 3}

Step 4. Bookmark the following stat blocks in the Monster Manual or on D&D Beyond:

  • @UUID[Actor.mmAnimatedArmor0]{Animated Armor}

  • @UUID[Actor.mmLacedonGhoul00]{Ghoul, Lacedon}

  • @UUID[Actor.mmShadow00000000]{Shadow}

Animals:

Adventure Background.name: Adventure Background
Adventure Background.text:
The fiendish, immortal mage Venger weaves interlocking schemes across the D&D multiverse to amass power and thwart his enemies. Some of Venger’s schemes involve allying with—or opposing—heroes he manipulates to his own ends.

To identify heroes who might prove useful in future plots, Venger has built tombs across the multiverse as testing grounds. When heroes’ deeds catch his attention, he invites those heroes to claim the treasure inside the tombs. Venger often challenges heroes to explore numerous tombs before he’s convinced of their usefulness.

The offer of treasure is real—though Venger considers the treasures in his tombs inconsequential, adventurers might find them worth the risk. But the tombs are deadly, and they’ve become the final resting place for many adventurers who’ve failed Venger’s challenges.

Among the earliest tombs Venger built is the @UUID[Scene.aunTombOfTheShad]{Tomb of the Shadow Serpents}. It’s situated within a cave on the Material Plane near an intersection with the Shadowfell, so strange and gloomy environs envelop the tomb. The tomb holds deadly monsters and traps. Surviving the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents is the first step toward earning Venger’s respect.

Adventure Hooks

For this adventure, your characters need to know only that a powerful individual has challenged them to explore the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents in search of treasure. You might make it clear that Venger has invited them, or you could obscure his identity, allowing the characters to deduce the tomb’s creator while they explore or even once they’ve completed the adventure.

If you want to further entice the characters, use one of the following adventure hooks to draw them into the story:

A Deadly Rivalry. The characters are embroiled in competition with another group and wish to prove their superior skills. Perhaps the characters are working for one of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunMagicalFactCQ]{magical factions} described in chapter 4 and wish to claim the tomb’s treasure before another faction does. Or perhaps the characters have caught wind that rivals who compete with them for quests are also headed toward the tomb, and the characters hope to claim its treasure first. Regardless of the details, the characters can claim treasure—and bragging rights—if they survive the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents.

Impress a Patron. The characters are cultivating a relationship with a powerful patron who might fund their continued adventures. Perhaps the characters want to impress a potential patron—such as one of the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunMagicalGrouiX]{group patrons} described in chapter 3—or they’re trying to cement a fledgling relationship with a patron. Either way, the patron loves magical lore and tales of adventure. Emerging victorious from the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents is sure to get the patron’s attention and prove the characters’ capabilities.

Beginning the Adventure.name: Beginning the Adventure
Beginning the Adventure.text:
The characters receive a message from Venger. This might reach the characters in a nonmagical way, such as a letter delivered by a messenger, or it might reach them via magic such as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMagicMouth]{Magic Mouth} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplProgrammed]{Programmed Illusion} spell.

For players excited to play an adventure involving Venger, consider beginning with a Programmed Illusion spell (spell save [[/check inv 19]]{DC 19}) that activates when the characters reach the forest in which the tomb is located. When the illusion activates, the characters see @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.S2e5LLp7ILJdQPqr]{a winged, one-horned fiend astride a flying black horse}. The fiend swoops down from above and delivers the message in a deep, booming voice before flying away again.

If the journey to the tomb is more than a short distance away, include directions in this message as necessary:

“Would-be heroes! Should you desire fame and treasure, heed this challenge. My Tomb of the Shadow Serpents lies nearby, built within a cave of unrelieved gloom. Seek out the stone doors that bear a serpent; within lies what you seek. “I eagerly await heroes worthy of claiming the tomb’s riches. Many die terrible deaths within, but perhaps you shall be different. Test your mettle in my tomb, and perhaps one day we shall meet again to our mutual benefit.”

If Venger’s message is delivered in writing, it is signed with a capital V.

Reaching the Tomb

Summarize the trip to the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents with this description:

The journey to the tomb is short and uneventful. As you venture further into the forest, the foliage becomes denser, and signs of folk living nearby or even passing through become scant. Soon, a hillock rises before you, and in its side yawns a gloomy cave maw. This must be the cave mentioned in the message!

The cave opening is @UUID[.T1CaveEntrancevj]{area T1}, which is described below.

TomboftheShado4Z.name: Tomb of the Shadow Serpents
TomboftheShado4Z.text: The Tomb of the Shadow Serpents has served Venger for generations as a testing ground for adventurers. Before inviting adventurers to brave it, Venger resets or repairs the tomb’s features and replenishes its treasure to ensure there are always challenges and rewards for heroes who survive it. He never gives another thought to those who die here, leaving their bodies to litter the tomb.

Conclusion.name: Conclusion
Conclusion.text:
Once the characters are finished exploring the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents, award each character [[/award 100XP each]] for completing the adventure. The characters should have enough XP to advance to level 2 by the end of the adventure. If you’re using a method of level advancement that doesn’t rely on XP, the characters gain a level after defeating the shadows in the sepulcher.

If the characters survive the Tomb of the Shadow Serpents, Venger notices their prowess. He tracks the characters throughout their adventuring careers and might challenge them to explore other tombs he’s created throughout the multiverse.

Dungeons in several published D&D adventures can be easily repurposed as tombs that Venger challenges the characters to explore. The temple in the level 4 adventure “The Will of Orcus” in Dragon Delves, for example, could be reimagined as such a tomb, with the cultists of the demon lord Orcus instead becoming sycophantic followers of Venger. The Tomb of the Nine Gods in Tomb of Annihilation, meant for level 9 adventurers, could similarly be reimagined as a complex created by Venger instead of the lich Acererak. The Tomb of Wayward Souls in Vecna: Eve of Ruin, another dungeon created by Acererak, is appropriate for level 16 characters. You can also create new tombs that Venger challenges the characters to explore.

At your discretion, after the characters have survived the dangers of numerous tombs, Venger might offer the characters mysterious jobs such as finding an item, stopping or delivering a shipment of goods, or protecting a public figure. These schemes should feed into Venger’s attempts to thwart the League of Malevolence, an odious assemblage of power-hungry villains led by Venger’s former lackey, the human mage Kelek. The characters shouldn’t trust Venger, but they might accept his jobs (which always pay well) out of curiosity or as part of a plan to double-cross him.
