Tomb Features.name: Tomb Features
Tomb Features.text:
The @UUID[Scene.aunTombOfTheShad]{Tomb of the Shadow Serpents} consists of a mix of rooms with carved stone walls and natural cave chambers. Areas @UUID[.T1CaveEntrancevj]{T1}, @UUID[.T5SpiderlingDe5b]{T5}, @UUID[.T8LacedonsLairgP]{T8}, @UUID[.T9WebbedTunnelAQ]{T9}, and @UUID[.T10SpidersNestTp]{T10} are cave chambers, while areas @UUID[.T2TombEntrywayLl]{T2}, @UUID[.T3DeadlyCorridM5]{T3}, @UUID[.T4MudPitxUTFZRG8]{T4}, @UUID[.T6LongCorridorQS]{T6}, @UUID[.T7HallofArmorQSF]{T7}, @UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{T11}, and @UUID[.T12TheShadowySeM]{T12} are constructed from stone.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.N7gAiGqj9Iw0lwiu cite=false]

The tomb has the following additional features.

Ceilings

The ceilings of the tomb’s cave chambers are 30 feet high. The ceilings of stone chambers are 20 feet high.

Doors

Doors are made of stone and unlocked, except for the door that leads to the sepulcher (@UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{area T11}), which is locked with the serpent puzzle described in @UUID[.#serpent-puzzle]{Serpent Puzzle}.

Fallen Adventurers

Throughout the tomb are the bodies of adventurers who have fallen to the place’s perils. These adventurers might be of any species appropriate for your setting—such as a mix of dwarves, humans, and orcs. Area descriptions include visual clues about how the adventurers died. Any character who notices a fallen adventurer can take the &Reference[Study] action to examine the body and make a [[/check 15 inv]] check; on a successful check, they determine the adventurer succumbed to a nearby trap—or to a nearby monster, as in @UUID[.T8LacedonsLairgP]{area T8}.

Lighting

In the tomb’s stone chambers and in its cave entrance, sconces shaped like shadowy serpents fill the area with &Reference[Dim Light]. The tomb’s interior cave chambers are areas of &Reference[Darkness]; descriptions of these areas assume characters have a way of seeing in the dark.

Serpent Puzzle

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.XxnK4wNzyTI0380z classes="float-right overlay-caption" cite=false]

The mosaic on the double door in @UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{area T11} that leads to the sepulcher is identical to the mosaic on the door in @UUID[.T1CaveEntrancevj]{area T1}. The mosaic is shown below. Each mosaic depicts a stylized, shadowy serpent. The mosaic on the sepulcher door, however, is missing three obsidian pieces that combine to form the shape of the serpent. These puzzle pieces are scattered throughout the tomb.

Serpent puzzle pieces are located in areas @UUID[.T6LongCorridorQS]{T6}, @UUID[.T8LacedonsLairgP]{T8}, and @UUID[.T10SpidersNestTp]{T10}, as shown on the map. Each puzzle piece is made from obsidian and worth 10 GP. A character who examines a piece realizes it’s a broken part of an obsidian mosaic identical to the one in the door that leads into the tomb. The characters must place the puzzle pieces correctly back into the broken mosaic (or bypass the puzzle; see @UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{area T11}) before they can enter the sepulcher.

Walls

The walls of cave chambers are made of earth and thick tree roots. The walls of stone chambers are made from slabs of solid stone.

Cave Entrance.name: Cave Entrance
Cave Entrance.text:
When the characters are ready to venture into the cave described in @UUID[.BeginningtheAdSF#reaching-the-tomb]{Reaching the Tomb}, read or paraphrase the following:

Three hulking, wolflike beasts lumber around this wide cave entrance, their red, malevolent eyes peering at you. Gray light flickering from sconces reflects off an obsidian mosaic in a double door at the back of the cave entrance. The mosaic depicts an S-shaped serpent.

Three @UUID[Actor.mmWorg0000000000]{Worgs} lurk here and begin combat when the characters move 10 feet into the cave.

The worgs recently adopted the cave entrance as their home, assuming that creatures living inside the double door would periodically emerge and provide the worgs with scrumptious meals. The characters are the worgs’ first potential victims, and the hungry creatures fight to the death. The worgs don’t know about Venger or care about the purpose of the tomb.

Serpent Mosaic. The obsidian serpent mosaic on the double door is one foot wide and one foot tall. It’s identical to the mosaic the characters must reconstruct to open the serpent puzzle door in @UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{area T11}.

Tomb Entryway.name: Tomb Entryway
Tomb Entryway.text:
A stone double door stands in the east wall of this chamber, and another stands in the west wall. Flanking the path that leads deeper into the temple are two identical statues. Each is seven feet tall and depicts a one-horned, winged man wearing robes and an ominous grin.

These statues depict Venger, as any character familiar with the mage easily recognizes. Any character unfamiliar with Venger can take the &Reference[Study] action to examine a statue and make a [[/check 10 skill=his/rel]] check to try to identify the statue’s likeness.

Statue Traps. The statues are magical traps. The first time a creature moves within 5 feet of a statue, that statue intones in a deep, commanding voice, “Clasp my hand for a boon.”

If a creature touches a statue’s hand, a fiery jolt of energy discharges and the creature makes a [[/save 12 dex]], taking [[/damage 1d10 fire average]] damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. On a success or failure, the statue’s magical voice chuckles and shouts, “Expect no favors!” Each statue activates only once.

Detecting the Traps. A @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDetectMagi]{Detect Magic} spell reveals an aura of Evocation magic around each statue. As a &Reference[Search] action, a creature within 5 feet of a statue can examine it and make a [[/check 10 prc]] check, noticing that the statue’s hand emits warmth. The traps can’t be disarmed, but they can be avoided by simply not touching the statues’ hands.

Deadly Corridor.name: Deadly Corridor
Deadly Corridor.text:
A desiccated corpse wearing rusty armor lies sprawled on this corridor’s floor. The circlet on the corpse’s head is strangely pristine and glints in the sconces’ light, and a serpent-shaped blade protrudes from the body. Double doors lead east, west, and south.

This T-shaped corridor leads deeper into the tomb.

Blade Traps. There are two pressure plates in this corridor, as denoted on the map. When a creature moves onto a pressure plate for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, a gap opens in the adjacent wall, and a serpent-shaped blade flies toward the creature. The creature on the plate must succeed on a [[/save dex 15]] saving throw or take [[/damage 1d6 slashing average]] damage. Each trap activates once per turn. Once a trap has activated three times, the trap ceases to function.

Detecting and Disarming the Traps. As a &Reference[Search] action, a creature can examine a section of floor that forms a pressure plate and make a [[/check 15 prc]] check, detecting the pressure plate on a successful check. Wedging an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagSpikesIron0]{Iron Spike} or similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

Fallen Adventurer. Except for the circlet, the fallen adventurer’s equipment is dented and unusable.

Treasure. The circlet on the corpse’s head is a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgCircletOfBlas]{Circlet of Blasting}.

Mud Pit.name: Mud Pit
Mud Pit.text:
Spanning most of this chamber is a large pit of bubbling mud, from which rise shimmering waves of heat. A rickety bridge made of chains and decaying wooden planks crosses the pit.

The chain bridge is &Reference[Difficult Terrain]. When a creature steps on the bridge for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a [[/save dex 12]] saving throw or fall into the mud pit. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

Mud Pit. The area of the mud pit acts like a 10-foot-deep @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgQuicksandPit0]{quicksand pit} hazard (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide, actor placed for ease of use), but the mud is also dangerously hot thanks to a natural underground hot spring. Any creature that starts its turn in the mud takes [[/damage 1d6 fire average]] damage.

Treasure. The western alcove is full of detritus covered in dried mud. A thorough search of the alcove takes 1 minute and yields a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgPotionOfFireB]{Potion of Fire Breath}.

Spiderling Den.name: Spiderling Den
Spiderling Den.text:
The air in this dark, enormous cave is cool and damp. Thick spiderwebs cover the center of the floor and the entrance to a tunnel leading away to the east. A lumpy, five-foot-wide sac of webbing bulges from the eastern wall next to the tunnel’s entrance.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.1j1NpFDgtyyByTZ2 classes="float-right overlay-caption" cite=false]

Six juvenile giant spiders (use the @UUID[Actor.mmGiantWolfSpide]{Giant Wolf Spider} stat block) lurk within the webs in the center of this chamber. They’re the young of the giant spiders in @UUID[.T10SpidersNestTp]{area T10}. A character who takes a &Reference[Search] action to survey the webs and succeeds on a [[/check 17 prc]] check notices the spiders.

As soon as a character ventures within 10 feet of the webs, the spiders emerge and begin combat. They fight to the death.

Webs. Areas covered in webs, as denoted on the map, use the rules for the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgWebs000000000]{webs} hazard (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide, actor placed for ease of use).

Egg Sac. The @UUID[Actor.aunEggSac0000000]{sac} on the eastern wall holds unhatched spider eggs. The sac has AC 10; HP 8; Vulnerability to Fire damage; and Immunity to Piercing, Poison, and Psychic damage. The sac is unaffected if the webs around it are destroyed.

Ten minutes after a character first enters this area, the eggs hatch and four @UUID[Actor.mmSpider00000000]{Spiders} emerge. The spiders fight the characters on sight.

Long Corridor.name: Long Corridor
Long Corridor.text:
On this corridor’s floor slump three corpses with darts protruding from their flesh. The center body clutches a shiny, black object in one hand.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.dDOifrPSeFAJ7bJJ classes="float-right" caption=false ]

Bloodstains splatter the floor of this hallway.

Dart Traps. There are three pressure plates in this corridor, as denoted on the map. Each pressure plate triggers a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgPoisonedDarts]{poisoned darts} trap (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide, Actor placed for ease of use).

Fallen Adventurers. The adventurers’ equipment is dented and unusable.

Serpent Puzzle Piece. The body in the center of the corridor clutches a piece of the serpent mosaic in @UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{area T11}. When the characters find this piece, show them the @UUID[Item.aun1SerpentPuzzl]{Serpent Puzzle Piece 1} handout.

Hall of Armor.name: Hall of Armor
Hall of Armor.text:
Resting on a dais at the west end of this chamber are two suits of shining plate armor. Each suit is arranged on a stand whose wooden base is adorned with silver filigree. A few stairs lead up to the dais.

Both suits are @UUID[Actor.mmAnimatedArmor0]{Animated Armor}. As soon as a character ventures within 5 feet of the stairs, the suits begin combat.

When a character is within 5 feet of an animated armor, they notice a seal etched on the armor’s chest that depicts the ominously grinning face of a one-horned fiend—identical to the faces of the statues of Venger in @UUID[.T2TombEntrywayLl]{area T2}.

Treasure. The wooden base of each armor stand includes a small drawer. The drawers are locked. As a &Reference[Utilize] action, a character can try to pick the lock using Thieve's Tools, doing so with a successful [[/check 15 dex slt tool=thief]].

The drawer in the south stand holds two @UUID[Item.aunObsidianStone]{obsidian stones} worth 10 GP each. The drawer in the north stand holds a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgTanBagofTrick]{Bag of Tricks} (tan).

Lacedons’ Lair.name: Lacedons’ Lair
Lacedons’ Lair.text:
This wide cavern’s walls are slick with trickling water that forms a murky, ten-foot-wide pool. To the east of the pool lies a one-armed corpse, next to which glints a shiny, black object. Strange gurgles emanate from the cavern’s western end.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.hjLZeJmXjcRqQkpQ classes=float-right caption=false]

Two @UUID[Actor.mmLacedonGhoul00]{Lacedon Ghouls} lurk in this cavern. One is around a corner in the western alcove, chewing on an arm it severed from the body in the northeast corner. Another is underwater in the pool, waiting to ambush trespassers.

As soon as a character ventures within 5 feet of the fallen adventurer or comes within 25 feet of the western wall, the underwater ghoul jumps out of the pool and fights them. The sounds of combat beginning alert the ghoul in the western alcove; that ghoul drops the arm it’s chewing on and joins the fight.

Fallen Adventurer. The ghouls killed an adventurer and have been snacking on the corpse, which is covered in bite marks. The adventurer’s equipment is dented and unusable.

Murky Pool. The pool is 5 feet deep and filled with cool, mineral-laden water.

Serpent Puzzle Piece. Next to the body is a piece of the serpent mosaic in @UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{area T11}. When the characters find this piece, show them the @UUID[Item.aun2SerpentPuzzl]{Serpent Puzzle Piece 2} handout.

Webbed Tunnel.name: Webbed Tunnel
Webbed Tunnel.text:
Thick spiderwebs cover the floor, walls, and ceiling of this tunnel.

The area of this tunnel is a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgWebs000000000]{webs} hazard (see the Dungeon Master’s Guide).

Spiders’ Nest.name: Spiders’ Nest
Spiders’ Nest.text:
Thick webs spill from this long cave’s western opening. Perched on gossamer mounds of webbing to the north and south are two enormous spiders with hairy legs. On the northeast wall, a severed hand suspended in the webs holds a shiny, black object.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.niyiuJM3e9Q4GXHt classes=float-right caption=false]

There are two @UUID[Actor.mmGiantSpider000]{Giant Spiders} here: one in the northeast corner and one in the southeast alcove. As soon as the characters enter this cave, the spiders fight them.

The spiders are hungry and fight to the death. They long ago ate the body the severed hand came from.

Serpent Puzzle Piece. The severed hand holds a piece of the serpent mosaic in @UUID[.T11SerpentPuzzfq]{area T11}. When the characters find this piece, show them the @UUID[Item.aun3SerpentPuzzl]{Serpent Puzzle Piece 3} handout.

Serpent Puzzle Door.name: Serpent Puzzle Door
Serpent Puzzle Door.text:
The stone double door at the west end of this hall bears a mosaic similar to the one outside the tomb. But the space that held an obsidian, S-shaped serpent in the entrance’s mosaic is empty in this one. Softly glowing blue lines illuminate the serpent-shaped void.

This door’s magical lock is linked to the mosaic. The glowing lines in the mosaic’s empty spaces thrum with magic.

Serpent Mosaic. The mosaic is one foot wide and one foot tall. Placing the three missing pieces of the mosaic’s obsidian serpent in the mosaic unlocks the door. The pieces are located in the long corridor (@UUID[.T6LongCorridorQS]{area T6}), the lacedons’ lair (@UUID[.T8LacedonsLairgP]{area T8}), and the spiders’ nest (@UUID[.T10SpidersNestTp]{area T10}).

Alternatively, a character can take a &Reference[Magic] action to trace the glowing lines and simulate the puzzle pieces’ correct placement. A character who does so makes a [[/skill arc 18]] check. On a successful check, the door unlocks.

The Shadowy Sepulcher.name: The Shadowy Sepulcher
The Shadowy Sepulcher.text:
Before you stands an eight-foot-tall central statue, around which swirl tendrils of wispy, black shadow. The statue is made of faceted obsidian and depicts entwined serpents whose heads rise toward the ceiling. On a dais to the west are three sarcophagi, their marble lids carved with the likenesses of warriors in repose.

Three @UUID[Actor.mmShadow00000000]{Shadows} lurk in this room, each hidden in one of the sarcophagi. As soon as a character ventures west of the serpent statue, the shadows emerge and begin combat.

The shadows arose from the bodies of adventurers Venger killed for betraying him. The mage then bound the shadows to this room. In a cruel act of irony, Venger built elaborate sarcophagi for the adventurers’ bodies and placed them here, taunting the shadows with the prospect of eternal rest.

Serpent Statue. Venger built the serpent statue and imbued it with magic he drew from the Shadowfell. As a result, the statue causes this room to behave as if the room were on that plane. It also causes the shadows to take on a serpentine appearance.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.book.JournalEntry.aunArtHandoutsG2.JournalEntryPage.evcQNq5PmTtW31oa classes=overlay-caption cite=false]

A character who enters this room must succeed on a [[/save 10 wis]] saving throw or be affected by despair. Roll on the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.tables.RollTable.dmgShadowfellDes]{Shadowfell Despair} table in the Dungeon Master’s Guide to determine the form the despair takes.

The statue has AC 15, HP 18, and Vulnerability to Radiant damage. If the statue is reduced to 0 HP, the Shadowfell stops affecting this room, and any despair effects on the characters end immediately.

A character who takes the &Reference[Study] action to examine the statue and succeeds on a [[/skill arc 15]] check understands how the statue is affecting the room and surmises that its connection to the Shadowfell gives it Vulnerability to Radiant damage.

Treasure. The sarcophagus lids are made of solid marble. A character can take a &Reference[Utilize] action to make a [[/skill ath 12]] check, lifting one of the lids on a successful check.

Inside each sarcophagus are the desiccated remains of an adventurer, whose equipment is rusted and unusable. The north sarcophagus also holds a @UUID[Item.aunBloodstone000]{bloodstone} worth 50 GP. The central sarcophagus holds a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgCubeOfSummoni]{Cube of Summoning}. The south sarcophagus holds three @UUID[Item.aunBloodstone000]{turquoises} worth 10 GP apiece.

Venger.name: Venger
Venger.text:
Corrupted Force of Evil

An immortal mage and Fiend with an implacable hatred for Tiamat, Venger seeks to rule nations by amassing sycophants and long-lost magical artifacts. Though his bat-like wings allow him to fly, Venger prefers to ride on his trusted flying steed, a Nightmare that lurks on the Ethereal Plane until it’s needed. Venger sends his adviser, Shadow Demon (Shadow Demon), to survey distant lands, then weaves interlocking plans based on Shadow Demon’s reports.

Venger was once a good-hearted human studying wizardry under the cryptic tutelage of his father. In time, Venger grew impatient and sought to increase his magical prowess by dabbling in minor pacts with demons. He eventually met demons who worshipped Tharizdun the Chained God, an entity the demons believed powerful enough to create whole planes of existence. Venger yearned to forge a pact with this entity, believing that doing so would give him immense power.

With the help of these Tharizdun-worshipping demons, Venger opened a brief window into the demiplane of Tharizdun’s imprisonment. The demons had neglected to mention that the souls of all who look on the Chained God face certain doom. As Venger gazed on this entity—an unknowable, indescribable blend of demonic and aberrant influence—Venger’s form warped, and the last traces of goodness sloughed off him. The demons collected this good essence and locked it in a vault that they spirited away to a distant corner of the Material Plane. Venger emerged from this encounter as a cruel, twisted version of himself, exalted now with immortality and magical might, and he vowed to free the Chained God.

At first, Venger earnestly pursued this promise. In time, though, he grew to despise his vow and neglected it in favor of his own pursuit of power. Now he no longer wants Tharizdun freed, knowing his disloyalty could make him a target of Tharizdun’s wrath.

After abandoning his quest to free Tharizdun, Venger sought to use several Orbs of Dragonkind to control Tiamat. This futile endeavor earned Venger Tiamat’s lifelong enmity. Venger now plots endlessly to destroy or subjugate Tiamat, among other nefarious designs. Roll on or choose a result from the Venger’s Schemes table to inspire Venger’s next power play.

@Embed[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.tables.RollTable.aunVengersSchebf rollable resultLabel="Venger Plots To …" captionPosition=top]{Venger's Schemes}

Veger’s Lairs

Venger keeps several lairs in each of the worlds he visits. Each is a castle perched above or extending from the side of a treacherous cliff, but none are identical.

Venger’s presence fouls the regions his lairs inhabit, creating the following effects:

Desolate Terrain. Plant life within 1 mile of a lair withers and dies, creating a barren wasteland of cracked dirt.

Tormented Rest. Abyssal whispers plague visitors’ dreams. Whenever a creature other than Venger or his allies finishes a Long Rest within 1 mile of a lair, it must succeed on a [[/save con 15 format=long]] or gain 1 &Reference[Exhaustion] level.

If Venger dies or moves a lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.
